@Willianvdv well I would love to have this working but I can't figure out a simple way to detect if a value is a really a react component :

* if it's a function it collides with the custom function that we can already use ( (data) => (string) vs (data) => (react stuff) )
* if it's an React Class, I don't know how to figure out if it's a constructor of a React Component or something else
* if it's an ES6 class, we might be more lucky because it will extend React.Component and we can use instanceof

What do you think? Am I missing something?
